:::{#exr-mle-use-log}
#### Comparing likelihoods through log-likelihoods

Suppose $\Lik(\param) > 0$ for every $\param$.
Determine how the parameter values that maximize the likelihood $\Lik$
relate to the parameter values that maximize the [log-likelihood](#def-loglik) $\lik$.
:::

{{< slidebreak >}}

:::{#sol-mle-use-log}

Let $\param^*$ be a parameter value.
The natural logarithm is strictly increasing on $(0, \infty)$,
so for any $\param_1$ and $\param_2$,
$\Lik(\param_1) \ge \Lik(\param_2)$ if and only if $\log \Lik(\param_1) \ge \log \Lik(\param_2)$,
that is, $\lik(\param_1) \ge \lik(\param_2)$.
So $\param^*$ satisfies $\Lik(\param^*) \ge \Lik(\param)$ for every $\param$
if and only if it satisfies $\lik(\param^*) \ge \lik(\param)$ for every $\param$.
So a parameter value $\param^*$ maximizes $\Lik$ if and only if it maximizes $\lik$.

:::
